new: Regional medullary redox indices and exploratory RT-qPCR findings in rats with atlantoaxial joint disorder

old: We examined regional medullary redox indices and Nox1/Nox4 transcripts in male Wistar rats with atlantoaxial joint disorder. Sham-operated and model rats were sampled at week 4; restoration rats underwent implant removal at week 4 and sampling at week 8. Each endpoint included six independent rats per group. In tissue containing the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM) and adjacent medulla, week-4 model rats had lower SOD activity, higher MDA and probe-associated fluorescence, and estimated Nox1/Nox4 expression of 1.46/2.90-fold relative to sham rats. old: A metallic implant in the rat atlantoaxial joint produces misalignment and blood-pressure elevation [1]. Oxidative stress is implicated in hypertension [2]; the rostral ventrolateral medulla (RVLM) regulates blood pressure [3], and experimental studies link regional redox disturbances to cardiovascular regulation [4,5]. We examined medullary biochemical indices and Nox1/Nox4 transcripts in this model. Blood-pressure observations were shared with a related Ang II/AT1-R report [6], whereas the present biochemical and transcript analyses were not reported there.

The Animal Ethics Committee of Anhui University of Chinese Medicine approved the 60-rat parent experiment, model induction, implant removal and terminal sampling (AHUCM-rats-2022032). Clean-grade male Wistar rats (approximately 12 weeks, 250 g; Anhui Medical University, license SCXK [Wan] 2017-001) were individually housed at 22 ± 1°C and 60% humidity under 12 h light/dark cycles, with free food/water and 1-week acclimatization. Animals were randomized to sham operation (10) or model induction (50). Six rats died intraoperatively and three afterward; seven survivors lost implants, leaving 34 with retained implants. Successfully modeled rats were randomized to model, restoration or superior cervical ganglion resection groups (10 each); four remained in reserve. Restoration rats continued from this successfully modeled cohort to week 8, while separate model rats underwent terminal sampling at week 4. This report includes sham, model and restoration cohorts only, initially 10 per group; each biochemical endpoint and RT-qPCR used six randomly selected independent rats per group without pooling. No single primary endpoint or formal a priori power calculation was specified. Animal-to-sample identifiers and cross-assay overlap could not be recovered.

Surgery used 2% inhaled isoflurane at 1 l/min, with respiratory, righting-reflex and noxious-withdrawal monitoring. An S-shaped aluminum implant was placed in the left atlantoaxial joint through an anterior cervical approach [1]; sham rats underwent exposure without implantation. Week-4 screening required retained implantation, joint asymmetry with a left–right odontoid–lateral-mass distance difference >0.05 mm, and systolic pressure ≥20% above baseline with a week-4 plateau. Restoration rats underwent implant removal at week 4. Penicillin sodium was given intramuscularly at 400,000–800,000 units/kg daily for 3 days. Possible contributors to the nine deaths were anesthetic overdose, cervical injury and infection; individual cause-of-death adjudication records were unavailable. No postoperative analgesics were administered; no written rationale or specific ethics-committee opinion about this omission was retained. Food intake, activity and wounds were checked daily for 3 days and 2–3 times weekly thereafter.

Sham/model rats were sampled at week 4 and restoration rats at week 8, without a time-matched second-surgery sham control. Abdominal aortic sampling under isoflurane was followed by inhaled-isoflurane overdose; death was confirmed when spontaneous breathing, palpable cardiac activity and withdrawal to a noxious stimulus were all absent, before brainstem removal. Atlas-guided bilateral tissue blocks (approximately 100 mg/rat) contained RVLM and adjacent medulla. For biochemical assays, tissue was lysed in RIPA/PMSF and protein measured by BCA. SOD (A001-3, WST-1) and MDA (A003-1, thiobarbituric acid; Nanjing Jiancheng) used RT-6000 absorbance readings at 450 and 530 nm, respectively; the MDA manual specified 532 nm. The fluorescence-reader model was not retained. BestBio BB-475015 O12 fluorescence was measured at excitation/emission 488/530 nm and divided by protein concentration, yielding an arbitrary-unit (AU) index. This serum-designated assay lacked tissue-matrix and buffer-compatibility validation; fluorescence is not an absolute ROS concentration or species-specific measure.

RNA extraction used TRIzol; reverse transcription used PrimeScript RR047A, followed by SYBR RT-qPCR on PikoReal 96. Each target and paired β-actin reference was measured once per rat, without technical replication. Within-rat ΔCq was target minus reference Cq. Relative quantity was calculated as Q = 2−ΔCq and divided by the arithmetic mean quantity of the six sham rats [7]. This assumes equal, approximately 100% amplification efficiencies. Original Cq, amplification and melting exports are provided in Supplementary File 7. Target melt profiles were heterogeneous; the authors confirmed two Plate annotation errors. Efficiencies and β-actin stability were not validated; no-template/no-reverse-transcription control records were unavailable. The six supplied records per group were retained unchanged for exploratory reporting. Reagent details, primers, protocols and source-flow information are retained in Supplementary Methods.

Individual rats were experimental units; results are mean ± sample SD. All six supplied values per group were included, without outlier removal or imputation. Biochemical comparisons used Welch ANOVA and Games–Howell tests, adjusting three comparisons within each endpoint, without adjustment across endpoints. RT-qPCR inference used Welch t tests on ΔCq, with Holm correction across all 18 comparisons in the original six-target panel, not only the displayed genes. Tests were two-sided (α = 0.05). Inputs, complete outputs, confidence intervals and code accompany the manuscript; cross-assay correlations were not tested.

Across the terminal cohorts, Welch ANOVA gave F(2, 9.816) = 91.626 for SOD, F(2, 8.500) = 130.738 for MDA and F(2, 7.804) = 314.907 for fluorescence (all P < 0.001). In week-4 model versus sham rats, SOD was 0.564 ± 0.072 versus 1.122 ± 0.072 U/mg protein, MDA 0.349 ± 0.034 versus 0.095 ± 0.017 nmol/mg protein, and fluorescence 3295.6 ± 216.3 versus 1326.9 ± 50.6 AU (Fig. 1; all Games–Howell-adjusted P < 0.001; Supplementary Table S1). Estimated Nox1 expression was 1.459 ± 0.156 versus 1.000 ± 0.134, and Nox4 2.902 ± 0.558 versus 1.000 ± 0.233 (Fig. 2; Holm-adjusted P = 0.0037 and 0.0001).

At the later restoration endpoint, SOD was 1.035 ± 0.101, MDA 0.213 ± 0.049 and fluorescence 2265.6 ± 131.6 in the same respective units; all differed from model values (adjusted P < 0.001). Relative to sham, MDA and fluorescence remained higher (P = 0.0033 and <0.001), whereas the SOD difference was nonsignificant (P = 0.2534). Restoration Nox1/Nox4 estimates were 1.180 ± 0.090/1.645 ± 0.227, lower than model values (adjusted P = 0.0139/0.0037). Compared with sham, Nox4 remained higher (P = 0.0099); Nox1 was nonsignificant (P = 0.0618). Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence or normalization. Full three-cohort statistics are supplied.

Lower SOD activity and higher MDA provide complementary regional antioxidant and lipid-peroxidation observations [8]. Together with estimated Nox1/Nox4 elevations, these findings extend the model's characterization [1] and are consistent with redox disturbances in other hypertension models [4,5]. Transcript abundance does not establish increased NOX protein, oxidase activity or sympathetic output. Unvalidated O12 fluorescence is auxiliary; common processing cannot exclude differential matrix effects. Archived H&E fields and blood-pressure records are descriptive only (Supplementary Figs. S1/S2), with unconfirmed histological animal counts and unreconstructed terminal blood-pressure cohorts.

Interpretation remains constrained by regional rather than RVLM-specific sampling, heterogeneous target melt profiles, incomplete validation and untraceable cross-assay identities. Later restoration observations confound implant removal with age, elapsed time, recovery and repeat anesthesia/surgery. Omission of postoperative analgesia raises animal-welfare concerns and possible pain/stress confounding. Small exploratory samples and male-only inclusion limit precision and generalizability. The same-day model–sham comparison supports a regional phenotype; validated assays, anatomical localization and time-matched controls are required to investigate NOX-dependent sympathetic mediation or an implant-removal effect.

old: 在大鼠寰枢关节植入金属异物可形成关节错位及血压升高模型[1]。氧化应激与高血压有关[2]；头端延髓腹外侧区（RVLM）参与血压调节[3]，实验研究提示区域氧化还原紊乱与心血管调控相关[4,5]。本研究检测该模型的延髓生化指标及Nox1/Nox4转录本。血压观察与相关Ang II/AT1-R论文共享[6]，而本稿生化及转录本分析未在该文报告。

安徽中医药大学动物伦理委员会批准了起始60只动物的来源实验、造模、异物取出及终末取材（AHUCM-rats-2022032）。清洁级雄性Wistar大鼠约12周龄、250 g，由安徽医科大学提供（许可证SCXK [皖] 2017-001），单笼饲养，温度22 ± 1℃、湿度60%、12 h光暗周期，自由进食饮水，适应1周。动物随机分至伪手术组10只或造模队列50只。术中死亡6只，术后死亡3只；存活动物中7只异物脱落，34只异物在位。造模成功动物随机分入模型、复位或颈上神经节切除组，每组10只；另4只留作备用。复位组从该造模成功队列中分出并继续观察至第8周，另设模型组于第4周终末取材。本报告仅纳入伪手术、模型及复位队列，初始各10只；每项生化检测及RT-qPCR各随机选取每组6只独立动物，无跨动物混样。未指定单一主要终点或进行正式事前功效计算。动物与样本身份及跨检测重叠关系无法恢复。
